live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): a ransomware-as-a-service gang, its claimed victims and its apparent exit
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, ran a ransomware-as-a-service business from late 2021. It hit firms and local governments, often with only its own claims as proof. In March 2024 BleepingComputer judged it was running an exit scam.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also tracked as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
Cybernews reports that the ransomware was first observed in late 2021. It was noted for using the Rust programming language.
Sygnia says the group surfaced in November 2021 and runs a ransomware-as-a-service model. Cybernews describes it as selling malware subscriptions to criminals.
BleepingComputer reports that ALPHV is believed to be a rebrand of the DarkSide and BlackMatter operations.
BleepingComputer cites an estimate that ALPHV took in at least $300 million in ransoms from more than 1,000 victims up to September 2023.

Named victims span many sectors. Reports list a mortgage lender (loanDepot), a life insurer (Prudential Financial), a dental and medical distributor (Henry Schein) and a Canadian software group (Constellation Software).
Public bodies were hit too. A report links the 2022 attack on Suffolk County, which disabled its 911 system, to the group. The city of Alexandria, Louisiana, was listed as a victim in 2023.
Cybernews reports that BlackCat claimed NJVC, an IT firm supporting US government and defense bodies, and then removed the listing. The breach is the gang's own claim.

Several reported victim figures are the gang's own claims. It said it took over 1 TB from Constellation Software and over 80 GB from Alexandria. It said it took over 130 GB from Estée Lauder without encrypting the network.
Sygnia investigated a 2023 attack it attributes to BlackCat or one of its affiliates. Initial access came through a compromised third-party vendor.

In that case the attacker spent weeks moving through the network. Sygnia names Cobalt Strike, the Stowaway proxy tool and Kerberoasting. Data was copied to cloud storage with Rclone, and extortion emails followed.
The usual pressure is to list the victim on a leak site and threaten to publish the data. In the NJVC case the gang said it would release data in stages every 12 hours.

In the MGM Resorts attack, AlphV said in its own statement that it kept super administrator access to MGM's Okta and launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors. DataBreaches relayed these claims without verifying them.
In the Suffolk County case, DataBreaches noted screenshots posted by BlackCat that appeared to show backup infrastructure. The group's admin said backups should have been removed.
DataBreaches reported that AlphV claimed it pressured a Viking Therapeutics employee into filing an SEC complaint about the breach. That claim is unconfirmed.
BleepingComputer reports that an international law enforcement operation seized ALPHV's Tor negotiation and leak sites in December 2023.

In February 2024 BleepingComputer cited unnamed sources linking the Change Healthcare attack to BlackCat. It could not confirm this independently, and BlackCat had not claimed the attack at that point.
In March 2024 BleepingComputer concluded the gang was running an exit scam. Its leak and negotiation sites were offline, and it offered its source code for $5 million.

The gang posted a fake FBI seizure banner. Europol and the NCA said they were not involved, and the FBI declined to comment. BleepingComputer says it is unclear whether the group will return under a new name.
The US State Department offered rewards of up to $10 million for information on ALPHV, plus $5 million for people linked to its attacks.
Treat a gang's leak-site claim as unverified until the victim or an investigator confirms it.
Review the access your outside vendors hold, and keep backups that an intruder cannot reach.
